title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Chips Paddle Back Out While Apple Drags the Dow
conditions.summary: A mixed Election Day session: chip stocks rebounded hard and lifted the Nasdaq, while Apple's margin outlook pulled the Dow lower. The 10-year yield climbed toward 5 percent after a hot job openings report.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.83% to 25,372.01.
The Dow fell 0.38%, or 197 points, to 51,786.72, and the Russell 2000 added 0.27% to 2,813.48.
Chips led a rebound after a heavy selloff: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 2.6%, with all 30 members higher.
Apple's weaker margin outlook and soft consumer and financial names weighed on the Dow.
Breadth was slightly negative; tech was the best sector, while materials and consumer staples lagged.
The Nasdaq hit about +1.1% early in the afternoon, faded into the last hour, then firmed at the bell.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: September job openings came in at 7.52 million, well above the 7.16 million expected; hires rose and layoffs fell.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 6 basis points to roughly 4.95%.
Oil swung after a reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, then eased on hopes for Qatar-mediated talks; WTI ended near $96.
Voters went to the polls in the midterm elections; prediction markets favored Democrats to win the Senate, with results due tonight.
No major Fed news today; the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in October with two members dissenting in favor of a hike.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: AEHR (Aehr Test Systems): +26.5% — record quarterly revenue and a higher full-year forecast.
FN (Fabrinet): +15.5% — record fiscal first-quarter revenue, up 51%.
FI (Fiserv): +12.5% — raised its cost-savings target and announced buybacks.
LSCC (Lattice Semiconductor): +11.0% — record revenue more than doubled from a year ago.
AAPL (Apple): -1.9% — record revenue, but its holiday-quarter margin outlook disappointed on rising memory costs.
SHOP (Shopify): -8.7% — revenue and merchandise volume came in a touch below estimates.
DT (Dynatrace): -14.7% — shares slid after its quarterly report.
IT (Gartner): -13.4% — shares sank after earnings.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Before the open: Shopify fell 8.7%, Zebra Technologies dropped 8.8% on margin worries, and Revvity rose 7.8% on a higher forecast.
Palantir slipped 1.7% after a beat, as new US contract bookings slowed.
Pfizer raised its full-year guidance and finished with a small gain.
After the close: AMD beat on earnings with data center revenue up 97%, and shares jumped in after-hours trading.
Also out tonight: Super Micro, Arista Networks, Amgen and Block.

sections.title: Business News
items: Binance said hackers took about $6.3 billion in digital assets; the FBI tied the attack to a North Korea-linked group.
Investors pulled over $1 billion from US-listed bitcoin funds over two days after the Binance hack.
Meta drew up to $58 billion in orders for a $15 billion bond sale, and S&P moved its outlook to negative.
Organigram agreed to buy Aurora Cannabis, sending Aurora up 22%.
Average US gasoline hit $4.14 a gallon, the highest ever on an Election Day, according to AAA and GasBuddy.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Midterm election results will be in focus at the open.
Data: trade balance at 7:30 AM CT, ADP jobs at 8:15 AM CT, ISM services at 9:00 AM CT, EIA crude inventories at 9:30 AM CT.
Before the open: Uber, McDonald's, CVS Health, Novo Nordisk and Datadog.
After the close: Qualcomm, Arm and AppLovin.
October jobs report arrives Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November third, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding into the water, it's Election Day, and the last set of the day just rolled in. Gus the wonder dog has been sitting on the voting line in the sand all afternoon. Give the crowd a howdy, Gus! Okay, here's the final set. The S and P five hundred rose about a third of a percent to seven thousand five hundred sixty-nine. The Nasdaq gained eight tenths of a percent to twenty-five thousand three hundred seventy-two. The Dow slipped about four tenths of a percent, down one hundred ninety-seven points, to fifty-one thousand seven hundred eighty-seven. Small caps in the Russell two thousand added about a quarter percent. The story was chips. After a gnarly selloff, the semiconductor index jumped more than two and a half percent, and every single one of its thirty members was up. Apple was the anchor on the Dow. Record revenue, but a softer margin outlook on rising memory costs, and the stock fell almost two percent. Breadth was a little negative, with tech on top and materials and staples lagging. Now the wind and weather. September job openings came in at seven and a half million, well above the seven point two million expected. Hot labor data plus high oil pushed the ten year yield up about six basis points, to around four point nine five percent. Oil swung on Iran headlines, a reported US strike early, then hopes for talks. West Texas crude ended near ninety-six dollars. The VIX eased to about twenty point eight. Gold fell about one percent, and bitcoin rose about one and a half percent. And votes are being counted tonight in the midterms. Over in the lineup, Aehr Test Systems caught the wave of the day, hanging ten all the way to the beach, up twenty-six and a half percent on record revenue. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Fabrinet rose fifteen and a half percent, Fiserv climbed twelve and a half percent on cost cuts and buybacks, and Lattice Semiconductor gained eleven percent. On the wipeout side, Shopify fell almost nine percent on a slight revenue miss, Dynatrace dropped almost fifteen percent, and Gartner sank thirteen percent. Palantir slipped almost two percent as new US contracts slowed. On the tide chart tonight, A M D beat on earnings, with data center revenue up ninety-seven percent, and the stock jumped after hours. Super Micro and Arista Networks also reported tonight. In beach talk, Binance says hackers grabbed about six point three billion dollars in crypto, and investors pulled over a billion dollars from bitcoin funds. Gas hit four dollars fourteen cents a gallon, the highest ever on an Election Day. Tomorrow's forecast, the election results land first. Then A D P jobs at eight fifteen A M Central and I S M services at nine A M Central. Uber and McDonald's report before the bell, and Qualcomm and Arm report after. The Friday jobs report is the big swell of the week. I'm stoked on that chip bounce, but a soul surfer waits for the full set before paddling in. Want me to call a wave for you? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Wax your board and catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
